card.title: Moving coil galvanometer, ammeter, and voltmeter

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A coil in a radial field deflects in proportion to current because N I A B balances the spring. A parallel shunt turns the movement into an ammeter, and a series resistor turns it into a voltmeter. The coil current at full scale stays the small movement current.

rows.text:
Governing equation for "Moving coil galvanometer, ammeter, and voltmeter" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
N I A B = k θ
Shunt S = I_g G / (I − I_g)

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A 1 mA movement is typical in these problems.  ·  Critical damping settles the needle in the shortest time without overshoot.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A moving-coil galvanometer carries a coil in a radial magnetic field. The torque is N I A B and does not change with angle, because the field is radial. A hairspring supplies a restoring torque k θ.  ·  At rest, N I A B = k θ, so the deflection is proportional to the current. The scale can be marked in equal current steps.

rows.text: Radial field  ·  Spring balance  ·  Ammeter shunt  ·  Voltmeter multiplier

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Torque balances a spring.  ·  The scale is linear in a radial field.  ·  A shunt makes an ammeter.  ·  A series resistor makes a voltmeter.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale at 1.0 mA. Find the shunt that lets it read 1.0 A at full scale.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: At equilibrium → A  ·  An ammeter shunt is connected → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The coil current must stay small. To measure a large current, a low-resistance shunt is connected in parallel with the galvanometer. Most of the current bypasses the coil.  ·  If the galvanometer has resistance G and full-scale current I_g, and the ammeter is to read I, the shunt is S = I_g G / (I − I_g). A larger range needs a smaller shunt.  ·  To make a voltmeter, a large resistor is connected in series. The instrument then draws little current and can be placed across a component. The series resistor is (V / I_g) − G for a full-scale voltage V.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The shunt is parallel.  ·  The voltmeter resistor is series.  ·  A smaller shunt gives a larger current range.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The radial field is what keeps the scale linear.  ·  Do not swap shunt and multiplier.  ·  The coil still carries only I_g at full scale.
